points.title: 童年与成长
points.description: 杰克逊·波洛克出生于怀俄明州科迪，是五个兄弟中最小的一个。他的父亲是一位土地测量员，母亲是一位教师。波洛克的童年因频繁搬家而动荡不安，先后在亚利桑那州和加利福尼亚州生活。这段经历塑造了他独立、叛逆的性格。1928年，他在洛杉矶的高中遇到了艺术家弗雷德里克·沃斯，这激发了他对艺术的兴趣。沃斯鼓励波洛克参观洛杉矶县艺术博物馆，并开始学习艺术基础。
points.descriptionEn: Jackson Pollock was born in Cody, Wyoming, the youngest of five brothers. His father was a land surveyor and his mother a teacher. Pollock's childhood was marked by frequent moves, living in both Arizona and California. This experience shaped his independent and rebellious character. In 1928, while in high school in Los Angeles, he met artist Frederick F. Schwankovsky, who sparked his interest in art. Schwankovsky encouraged Pollock to visit the Los Angeles County Museum of Art and begin studying art fundamentals.

points.title: 艺术学习初期
points.description: 1930年，波洛克跟随哥哥查尔斯移居纽约，进入艺术学生联盟学习，师从托马斯·哈特·本顿。本顿的写实风格和动态构图对波洛克早期作品产生了深远影响。在此期间，波洛克也接触了墨西哥壁画家迭戈·里维拉和何塞·克莱门特·奥罗斯科的作品，他们的壁画规模和社会主题给他留下深刻印象。1938年，波洛克获得联邦艺术项目的工作，参与壁画创作，这使他有机会探索更大的尺度和更自由的创作方式。同时，他开始接触超现实主义艺术，特别是马克斯·恩斯特的作品，这为他后来的滴画技法埋下伏笔。
points.descriptionEn: In 1930, Pollock moved to New York with his brother Charles and enrolled in the Art Students League, studying under Thomas Hart Benton. Benton's realistic style and dynamic compositions profoundly influenced Pollock's early work. During this period, Pollock also encountered the work of Mexican muralists Diego Rivera and José Clemente Orozco, whose large-scale, socially themed murals left a deep impression on him. In 1938, Pollock secured a position with the Federal Art Project, where he worked on murals, allowing him to explore larger scales and more free-form approaches. Concurrently, he began engaging with Surrealist art, particularly the work of Max Ernst, which would later inform his drip painting technique.

points.title: 突破性发展
points.description: 1940年代，波洛克在格林尼治村的艺术圈中逐渐崭露头角。他与李·克拉斯纳(Lee Krasner)相遇并结婚，克拉斯纳成为他艺术生涯中的重要支持者和批评者。这一时期，波洛克开始摆脱传统绘画技法的束缚，探索非具象表现。他受到心理学家卡尔·荣格的集体无意识理论影响，试图通过艺术表达潜意识。1943年，佩吉·古根海姆(Peggy Guggenheim)给予波洛克首次个人展览的机会，并委托他创作壁画《壁画》(Mural)。这幅大型作品标志着波洛克艺术风格的重大转变，展现了他对动作和空间的全新理解。1945年后，波洛克开始发展其标志性的滴画技法，将画布铺在地板上，用棍棒或直接从颜料罐中滴洒颜料，创造出前所未有的抽象表现主义作品。
points.descriptionEn: During the 1940s, Pollock emerged in the art circles of Greenwich Village. He met and married Lee Krasner, who became an important supporter and critic throughout his artistic career. During this period, Pollock began breaking free from traditional painting techniques, exploring non-representational expression. Influenced by Carl Jung's theory of the collective unconscious, he sought to express the subconscious through his art. In 1943, Peggy Guggenheim gave Pollock his first solo exhibition and commissioned him to create the mural 'Mural.' This large-scale work marked a significant shift in Pollock's artistic style, showcasing his new understanding of movement and space. After 1945, Pollock developed his signature drip painting technique, laying canvases on the floor and dripping or splattering paint directly from cans, creating unprecedented Abstract Expressionist works.

points.title: 巅峰时期
points.description: 1947年，波洛克和妻子李·克拉斯纳搬到纽约长岛的斯普林斯(Spring)地区，这里成为他创作生涯的巅峰之地。在特洛伊工作室(Trovy Studio)中，波洛克完善了他的滴画技法，创作了一系列标志性的作品，包括《薰衣草之雾》(Lavender Mist)、《秋韵》(Autumn Rhythm)和《蓝柱》(Blue Poles)等。这些作品以其独特的构图、动态的线条和丰富的色彩层次，开创了绘画艺术的新纪元。波洛克将画布铺在地板上，围绕画布行走，从各个角度滴洒颜料，创造出复杂而有机的图案。这种创作方式被称为'行动绘画'(Action Painting)，强调创作过程本身的艺术价值。1948年，艺术评论家克莱蒙特·格林伯格(Clement Greenberg)开始大力推崇波洛克的艺术，使他在艺术界获得广泛认可。1950年代，波洛克的作品在国际上展出，成为美国抽象表现主义的代表人物。
points.descriptionEn: In 1947, Pollock and his wife Lee Krasner moved to Springs on Long Island, New York, which became the site of his most productive period. In his studio (later known as 'The Pollock-Krasner House and Study Center'), Pollock perfected his drip painting technique, creating a series of iconic works including 'Lavender Mist,' 'Autumn Rhythm,' and 'Blue Poles.' These pieces, with their unique compositions, dynamic lines, and rich color layers, pioneered a new era in painting. Pollock laid his canvases on the floor, walking around them and dripping paint from various angles, creating complex, organic patterns. This approach, dubbed 'Action Painting,' emphasized the artistic value of the creative process itself. In 1948, art critic Clement Greenberg began championing Pollock's work, bringing him widespread recognition in the art world. During the 1950s, Pollock's work was exhibited internationally, establishing him as a leading figure of American Abstract Expressionism.

points.title: 晚年与逝世
points.description: 1950年代中期，波洛克的创作生涯开始走下坡路。他受到酒精问题的严重困扰，情绪波动极大，创作数量和质量都显著下降。1953年后，他尝试回归画架绘画，但未能重现早期的创新活力。1956年8月11日，波洛克在酒后驾车失控，撞上附近的一棵树，不幸身亡，年仅44岁。他的去世标志着美国抽象表现主义黄金时代的结束。波洛克去世后，他的艺术成就得到更广泛的认可，1956年纽约现代艺术博物馆举办了回顾展，进一步巩固了他在艺术史上的地位。他的妻子李·克拉斯纳在他去世后致力于保护他的艺术遗产，建立了波洛克-克拉斯纳基金会，确保他的作品得到妥善保存和研究。波洛克的创新技法和对艺术边界的突破，使他成为20世纪最具影响力的艺术家之一。
points.descriptionEn: In the mid-1950s, Pollock's career began to decline. He struggled severely with alcoholism, experiencing extreme mood swings, and both the quantity and quality of his work diminished significantly. After 1953, he attempted a return to easel painting but failed to recapture his earlier innovative vitality. On August 11, 1956, Pollock died in a car accident while driving under the influence, crashing into a tree near his home. He was only 44 years old. His death marked the end of the golden age of American Abstract Expressionism. After his death, Pollock's artistic achievements gained even wider recognition. In 1956, the Museum of Modern Art in New York held a retrospective exhibition, further cementing his place in art history. His wife Lee Krasner, after his death, dedicated herself to preserving his artistic legacy, establishing the Pollock-Krasner Foundation to ensure his works were properly preserved and studied. Pollock's innovative techniques and breakthrough of artistic boundaries have made him one of the most influential artists of the 20th century.

supporter.zh: 波洛克被艺术界视为革命性的创新者，他彻底改变了绘画的可能性。他的行动绘画技法打破了传统绘画的束缚，将艺术创作从具象表现转向抽象表达，开创了抽象表现主义的新纪元。波洛克的作品体现了美国艺术的独立性和原创性，使美国艺术首次摆脱了欧洲的影响，获得了国际认可。他的创作过程本身就是一种艺术形式，强调身体动作与画布的直接互动，这种理念影响了后世无数艺术家。波洛克的艺术遗产不仅体现在他的作品上，更在于他拓展了艺术的边界，为后来的艺术发展开辟了新的可能性。
supporter.en: Pollock is regarded by art supporters as a revolutionary innovator who fundamentally transformed the possibilities of painting. His action painting technique shattered the constraints of traditional art, shifting artistic expression from representation to abstraction, pioneering a new era in Abstract Expressionism. Pollock's work embodied the independence and originality of American art, enabling American art to break free from European influence for the first time and gain international recognition. His creative process itself became an art form, emphasizing the direct interaction between physical movement and canvas, an idea that influenced countless subsequent artists. Pollock's artistic legacy is not only evident in his works but also in his expansion of artistic boundaries, opening new possibilities for future artistic development.

critic.zh: 批评者认为波洛克的艺术存在严重缺陷。首先，他的作品被指责为缺乏技巧和深度，仅仅是随意泼洒颜料的结果，而非深思熟虑的艺术创作。其次，波洛克的个人生活充满争议，尤其是他的酗酒问题和婚姻问题，这些负面特质常常被与其艺术成就联系在一起。此外，一些评论家认为波洛克的艺术被过度商业化，艺术市场对他的炒作掩盖了作品本身的不足。批评者还指出，波洛克的创新被过度夸大，实际上他受到了多位欧洲现代艺术家的影响，如毕加索和米罗，他的'原创性'值得质疑。最后，波洛克晚期的作品质量明显下降，这反映了个人问题对其创作的负面影响。
critic.en: Critics argue that Pollock's art has significant flaws. First, his work is accused of lacking technical skill and depth, being merely the result of randomly splashed paint rather than thoughtful artistic creation. Second, Pollock's personal life was controversial, particularly his alcoholism and marital issues, which are often linked to his artistic achievements. Additionally, some critics believe Pollock's art was over-commercialized, with the art market's hype overshadowing the shortcomings of the work itself. Critics also point out that Pollock's innovation was overstated, as he was influenced by several European modern artists such as Picasso and Miró, making his 'originality' questionable. Finally, Pollock's late works showed a clear decline in quality, reflecting the negative impact of his personal problems on his creativity.

objective.zh: 从历史和流行文化视角看，波洛克已成为美国现代艺术的标志性人物。他的滴画技法不仅是一种艺术创新，更成为美国战后文化自信的象征。在艺术史上，波洛克被公认为抽象表现主义的领军人物，他的作品代表了艺术从欧洲中心向美国中心的转移。波洛克的形象已经超越了艺术领域，成为流行文化中的文化符号，出现在电影、时尚和广告中。他的生活故事，包括与李·克拉斯纳的关系、与艺术评论家的互动以及悲剧性的早逝，都成为艺术传奇的一部分。然而，客观评价必须承认，波洛克的成就既有创新的一面，也有争议的一面，他的艺术遗产是复杂而多维的，需要放在特定的历史和文化背景中理解。
objective.en: From a historical and pop culture perspective, Pollock has become an iconic figure in American modern art. His drip painting technique represents not only artistic innovation but also a symbol of American post-war cultural confidence. In art history, Pollock is widely recognized as a leading figure of Abstract Expressionism, and his work represents the shift of the art world's center from Europe to America. Pollock's image has transcended the art world, becoming a cultural symbol in popular culture, appearing in films, fashion, and advertising. His life story, including his relationship with Lee Krasner, interactions with art critics, and tragic early death, have all become part of art legend. However, an objective evaluation must acknowledge that Pollock's achievements have both innovative and controversial aspects, and his artistic legacy is complex and multidimensional, requiring understanding within its specific historical and cultural context.

self.zh: 绘画不是关于画架、画笔和颜料的事情，而是关于理念的事情。
self.en: Painting is not about easels, brushes and paint, it's about ideas.

others.zh: 波洛克是唯一一位真正改变了绘画方式，并改变了我们看待绘画方式的艺术家。
others.en: Pollock is the only artist who has really changed the way we look at painting and the way we paint.
